open_points.subject: Registry frontend credential trust boundary
open_points.text: How the frontend obtains the staff credential belongs to the frontend.
open_points.question: When the Registry frontend calls the API directly from a browser, is that browser trusted to receive and hold the shared staff credential, or must staff actions pass through a credential-holding frontend server?
options: The browser receives and presents the staff credential
Only a frontend server holds the credential and performs staff calls
Direct-browser use permits only unauthenticated reads
open_points.default_guess: Only a frontend server holds the credential and performs staff calls.

open_points.subject: Configuration startup contract
open_points.text: A change takes effect when the instance restarts
open_points.question: Which configuration entries are mandatory, and what observable result occurs when a required credential, token mapping or frontend origin is absent or invalid at restart?
options: Registry refuses to start with a configuration error
Registry starts but disables the affected capability
Registry ignores invalid entries and uses defaults
open_points.default_guess: Registry refuses to start with a configuration error.

open_points.subject: Deployment exposure check
open_points.text: the owner checks it when deploying
open_points.question: What concrete check establishes that Registry is unreachable beyond its host, what result records success, and what must happen when the check fails?
options: Inspect the effective bind and port-publication configuration
Run a reachability test from outside the host
Require both configuration inspection and an external reachability test
open_points.default_guess: Require both configuration inspection and an external reachability test, and reject the deployment if either fails.

open_points.subject: Secret generation
open_points.question: What makes a generated service token or staff credential acceptable, and what happens if the supplied value does not meet that requirement?
options: Require a specified amount of cryptographically random entropy
Require a defined encoded token format and length
open_points.default_guess: Require a defined encoded token format containing at least 256 bits of cryptographically random entropy and reject invalid configuration at startup.
